title: TRUMP and MELANIA Memecoins: The Presidential Pump-and-Dump That Made $100M in Fees
description_short: TRUMP and MELANIA Memecoins: The Presidential Pump-and-Dump That Made $100M in Fees
description_medium: Donald Trump launched the $TRUMP token two days before taking office; its rapid rise generated nearly $100 million in trading fees for affiliated entities within two weeks, Reuters reported. Melania Trump launched a second token two days later, with insiders holding most of its supply, according to the supplied analysis. Small traders lost money as prices fell. The launches tied presidential branding to speculative products that benefited connected holders.
description_long: On January 17, 2025 — two days before his inauguration — Donald Trump posted on Truth Social announcing the launch of the $TRUMP memecoin, which surged from an opening price of $0.18 to a peak of $75 within 24 hours, generating a market cap exceeding $14.5 billion at its apex. An early trader who purchased 5.97 million tokens within two minutes of the announcement — possibly tipped off in advance, forensic analysts told Wired — walked away with a profit of up to $109 million in two days. Entities behind the coin, including CIC Digital, a Trump affiliate controlling 80% of the token supply, accumulated nearly $100 million in trading fees within two weeks alone, according to analyses by blockchain firms Merkle Science and Chainalysis. The First Lady launched the $MELANIA coin on January 19, with insiders holding 89% of supply in what blockchain analytics firm Bubblemaps identified as a classic pump-and-dump structure. Former White House communications director Anthony Scaramucci warned: Now, anyone globally can effectively deposit money into the bank account of the President of the United States with just a few clicks. Every favor — be it geopolitical, corporate, or personal — is now openly for sale. By mid-2025, Trump's 2026 financial disclosure revealed CIC Digital had taken in over $600 million from meme coin sales, while retail investors bore catastrophic losses as the coins collapsed more than two-thirds from peak.

title: Trump University Forced to Drop “University” Name for Lack of License
description_short: Trump University Forced to Drop “University” Name for Lack of License
description_medium: New York State education officials told Trump that his business could not call itself a “university” because it lacked a license and did not meet legal definitions. The program was renamed the Trump Entrepreneur Institute in 2011. The episode underscored regulatory concerns about how the business was marketed to consumers.

title: House Republicans Launch Baseless Biden Impeachment Inquiry
description_short: House Republicans Launch Baseless Biden Impeachment Inquiry
description_medium: On September 12, 2023, Speaker Kevin McCarthy announced a formal Biden impeachment inquiry under pressure from Trump and MAGA House members, without a House vote. Republicans on the Oversight Committee led by James Comer and Jim Jordan had spent months investigating and found no direct evidence of Biden wrongdoing. Critics called the inquiry a retaliatory political maneuver designed to distract from Trump multiple criminal indictments. The inquiry produced no articles of impeachment.
description_long: On September 12, 2023, Speaker Kevin McCarthy announced a formal impeachment inquiry into President Joe Biden without first holding a House vote on opening one. The announcement followed pressure from Donald Trump and House Republicans who wanted an investigation of Biden and his family. Committees led by Oversight chair James Comer and Judiciary chair Jim Jordan had already spent months examining the allegations. The supplied account says their work found no direct evidence that Biden had committed wrongdoing. The inquiry nonetheless gave the allegations a formal congressional investigation, a step critics described as political retaliation and a way to shift attention from Trump’s criminal indictments. McCarthy’s announcement did not itself impeach Biden, and the inquiry produced no articles of impeachment. The episode therefore ended without a House impeachment vote based on its findings. Its central dispute was whether the investigation reflected evidence of misconduct or partisan use of Congress’s investigative authority.

title: NY Civil Fraud Trial - $355M penalty + interest (Feb 16, 2024)
description_short: Judge Engoron found Trump liable for persistent business fraud, imposing a $355M+ penalty and banning Trump and his sons from running NY businesses for years.
description_medium: On February 16, 2024, New York Judge Arthur Engoron found Donald Trump liable for persistent business fraud and ordered a penalty exceeding $355 million, plus interest. The ruling also barred Trump and his sons from running New York businesses for a period, combining financial liability with restrictions on business operations.

title: Trump calls for military tribunals for political opponents (2024)
description_short: In interviews and on Truth Social, Trump floated using military courts to try political enemies including former officials and media figures, a hallmark of authoritarian regimes.

title: Trump Admits in Deposition to Lying About Net Worth
description_short: Trump Admits in Deposition to Lying About Net Worth
description_medium: In a 2007 deposition in his lawsuit against journalist Timothy O’Brien, Donald Trump said his claimed net worth could change with his emotions and attitude. O’Brien had reported a far lower figure. The case was dismissed in 2011, and Trump’s sworn explanation later became relevant to scrutiny of his financial statements.
description_long: Donald Trump gave the deposition in 2007 while suing journalist Timothy O’Brien over reporting that Trump’s net worth was between $150 million and $250 million. Under oath, Trump said his estimate could fluctuate depending on how he felt emotionally and on his general attitude at the time. The testimony described a self-reported valuation that was not fixed to asset values alone. Trump’s lawsuit was dismissed in 2011. Years later, the deposition drew renewed attention during scrutiny of financial statements Trump submitted to banks and insurers in New York. The supplied account says the testimony became central to the state’s fraud case, where the accuracy of those statements was at issue. The deposition does not by itself establish every later misrepresentation, but it records Trump explaining how he arrived at a stated net worth in a sworn legal setting. The episode connects his public wealth claims, his challenge to O’Brien’s reporting, and subsequent questions about financial representations.

title: Ends Birthright Citizenship by Executive Order
description_short: Ends Birthright Citizenship by Executive Order
description_medium: In a blatant challenge to the 14th Amendment, Trump signed an executive order on January 20, 2025, attempting to end birthright citizenship for children born in the US to undocumented parents. The order was immediately blocked by federal courts as unconstitutional, but it served as a red meat political statement to his base and a direct assault on established constitutional rights.
description_long: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump signed an executive order seeking to deny U.S. citizenship at birth to some children born in the country to parents without lawful status. The order directed the executive branch to change how it recognized citizenship under the Fourteenth Amendment; it did not amend the Constitution. Federal courts quickly blocked the policy from taking effect, so the immediate result was a legal confrontation over the order rather than an end to birthright citizenship. The dispute concerned the amendment’s Citizenship Clause and the administration’s authority to narrow its application by executive action. The policy would have changed how the federal government treated a class of children born in the United States, with consequences for recognition of their citizenship. For affected families, any change would have shaped whether children received recognition as citizens at birth, although that consequence remained prospective while courts blocked implementation. The later appellate outcome is not stated.

title: Trump Withdraws US from World Health Organization
description_short: Trump Withdraws US from World Health Organization
description_medium: On his first day back in office, January 20, 2025, Trump signed an executive order withdrawing the United States from the World Health Organization. The move cut off US funding, which had constituted roughly 18% of WHO's budget, crippling global disease surveillance programs. Public health officials warned the withdrawal would leave the US blind to emerging pandemic threats. The move damaged US standing in global health governance and left a vacuum China moved to fill. Congress had no role despite having ratified US WHO membership through legislation.
